start.text: Down the ruts from the bend's lantern the hollow opens, and there's a sound in it you haven't heard here: a rake, drawn through charcoal, and drawn again.
The ruts bend, and you're in the hollow before you know you've found it. Her light's by the door. And there's a sound you haven't heard here: a rake, drawn through charcoal, and drawn again.

Wenna has the clamp's front raked open to the hearth. The inside is black, stick on stick, and a fan of it lies drawn out on the moss in front of her. Four sacks stand tied at the side. A fifth sits open at her feet.
Don't stand in my dust. It's a sack at a time, this. Always was. You can't hurry a burn and you can't hurry the breaking.
She draws the rake through again, slowly, and looks at what it brings out the way Ottie looks at his boots.
